historical_observations: The page shows how Swiss textile trade was distributed. Basle and Zurich were the centres for silk trading and manufacture, while St. Gallen, Glarus and Thalwil hosted production sites.

The Swiss Silk Bolting Cloth Manufacturing Co. Ltd. appears twice, under Screen Printing Silk and Silk Bolting Cloth. Its products served both the milling industry and screen printing, including pure silk and synthetic yarns.
Mentions of 'synthetic yarns' and 'man-made fibres' point to the post-war shift from natural silk to synthetics.
The directory is aimed at foreign buyers. It is in English, and Beltex lists a London office.
Tavaro's 'Elna' sewing machine is a well-known Swiss consumer export product.
